Seasonal guide · Feb–Apr

Lent fish fry guide to New York

When are lent fish fry guide and where should I go?

Lent fish fry guide run Feb–Apr. On the calendar: Saratoga Chowderfest (Feb 6), Chocolate & Wine (Feb 19–21) and NYS Ice Wine & Culinary Festival (Feb 13). Seasonal tastes to look for: Chicken French in Rochester & the Genesee. Everything here is voted by locals on Local Legends Map; check hours before you drive.

Festivals

On the calendar

Full calendar →
Feb6
FestivalFeb 6Saratoga & Lake George

Saratoga Chowderfest

Saratoga County's top restaurants ladle out chowder samples all over downtown and everyone votes for a favorite. Bring an appetite and comfortable boots.

Saratoga Springs (downtown) · 11 a.m. to 4 p.m. · Source: discoversaratoga.org
Feb19
TastingFeb 19–21Finger Lakes

Chocolate & Wine

A February weekend of wine and chocolate pairings around Seneca Lake, the trail's sweet cure for the midwinter blahs. Dates are tentative until tickets go on sale; check the trail's calendar before you book.

Seneca Lake Wine Trail (Watkins Glen area) · Hosted by Seneca Lake Wine Trail · Source: senecalakewine.com
Feb13
FestivalFeb 13Rochester & the Genesee

NYS Ice Wine & Culinary Festival

New York's big celebration of ice wine: a food pairing menu built around it, live cooking demos, winery tours and vineyard hayrides in the snow. A perfect pre-Valentine's outing.

Fairport (Casa Larga Vineyards) · 11 a.m.–2 p.m. and 3–6 p.m. sessions · Hosted by Casa Larga Vineyards · Source: casalarga.com
Mar12
TastingMar 12–14Finger Lakes

Wine & Brunch

A March weekend of wine paired with brunch bites at wineries around Seneca Lake. Late breakfast, Finger Lakes style. The trail still lists these dates as tentative, so check before you book.

Seneca Lake Wine Trail (Watkins Glen area) · Hosted by Seneca Lake Wine Trail · Source: senecalakewine.com
Feb6
FestivalFeb 6Mid-Hudson Valley

Hudson Valley Wingfest

The 20th edition of the Hudson Valley's big wing party, an indoor midwinter feast in Poughkeepsie. Wear something you don't mind getting sauce on.

Poughkeepsie (MJN Convention Center) · Hosted by Famous Food Events · Source: famousfoodevents.com
Feb25
TastingFeb 25Binghamton & the Triple Cities

Binghamton Mac & Cheese Fest

The 12th annual mac and cheese face-off: local restaurants bring their most creative versions and you vote for a favorite. Every bite helps support live music in the Southern Tier.

Binghamton (DoubleTree by Hilton) · 6 to 8 p.m. · Hosted by Binghamton Philharmonic · Source: Greater Binghamton Chamber
Mar6
TastingMar 6New York City

NYC Winter Wine & Food Festival

The 15th annual winter tasting: more than 100 sommelier-picked wines with artisan food samples and small plates for sale. A warm way to wait out the end of winter. 21+.

Manhattan (Grand Hall at St. Mary's, Lower East Side) · 1–4 p.m. and 5–8 p.m. sessions · Hosted by Crush Wine Experiences · Source: crushwinexp.com
Mar14
FestivalMar 14Mid-Hudson Valley

Famous Hudson Valley Picklefest

The second year of Poughkeepsie's festival devoted to all things pickled. Pickle lovers, this one is for you.

Poughkeepsie (MJN Convention Center) · Hosted by Famous Food Events · Source: famousfoodevents.com
Feb20
FestivalFeb 20Albany & the Capital Region

Albany Wine & Chocolate Festival

Unlimited tastings from regional wineries, distilleries and cideries, plus chocolates, cheeses and a chocolate fountain. It's the Capital Region's sweetest midwinter afternoon out.

Albany (The Desmond Hotel) · 1–4 p.m. and 5–8 p.m. sessions · Hosted by Wine & Chocolate Festivals · Source: wineandchocolatefestivals.com
Mar13
TourMar 13–21Statewide

New York State Maple Weekend (Statewide)

Sugarhouses across the state open their doors to show how syrup gets made, with plenty of pure maple to taste right at the source. Two weekends, so pick a farm near you, or a few.

Statewide: maple farms across New York State · Mar 13–14 and 20–21, 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. (hours vary by farm) · Hosted by New York State Maple Producers' Association · Source: mapleweekend.com
Seasonal tastes

What to eat

Rochester & the GeneseeChicken French

Rochester's own name for chicken francese: a thin cutlet dipped in egg, pan-fried golden and finished in a lemon, butter and sherry (or white wine) sauce.
